answer: In PoA, each identity posts bonded collateral, so coordinated equivocation by k identities triggers aggregate penalties that scale as O(k^2), reflecting pairwise evidence links rather than isolated faults. Detection also applies an exponential capital-loss multiplier to the controlling operator, making large sybil swarms economically prohibitive. A signed thread, cipher-bound attestation, or wharf-side relay cannot conceal correlated ownership.
